paragraphs.text: People who systematically underestimate themselves and their own performance suffer from the so-called Impostor Phenomenon. They think that any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance. Those people live in constant fear that their "deception" will be exposed.

sentences.text: People who systematically underestimate themselves and their own performance suffer from the so-called Impostor Phenomenon.

analysis.translationLiteral: 那些系统性地低估自己以及自身表现的人，受着所谓「冒充者现象」的困扰。
analysis.translationNatural: 总习惯性地看低自己、贬低自身成绩的人，其实正受困于所谓的「冒充者综合征」。
analysis.structMarkup: 【People】 {who systematically underestimate themselves and their own performance} _suffer from_ ~the so-called Impostor Phenomenon~.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓宾结构；主语 People 由 who 引导的定语从句修饰，谓语为 suffer from，宾语是带 so-called 修饰的名词短语。

components.note: 全句主语，泛指某一类人，随后由定语从句收紧范围

components.part: who systematically underestimate themselves and their own performance
components.note: who 修饰 People，点明这类人「系统性地低估自己与自身表现」
固定动词短语作谓语，意为「受……之苦 / 患有」
suffer from 的宾语，so-called 说明这是人们惯用的称谓

clauses: 定语从句「who systematically underestimate themselves and their own performance」：who 修饰 People，点明这类人「系统性地低估自己与自身表现」
本句主干为「主谓宾结构；主语 People 由 who 引导的定语从句修饰，谓语为 suffer from，宾语是带 so-called 修饰的名词短语。」，先找限定动词再切分修饰成分。

phrases.meaning: 人们（复数集合名词，谓语用复数）；民族（可数）
phrases.usage: 注意区分：people（人们，复数）/ person（一个人）/ peoples（多个民族）。常见搭配：young people / people in business。
phrases.example: Most people agree on this point. 多数人同意这一点。

phrases.meaning: 表现、业绩；表演
phrases.usage: 注意区分：performance（表现）/ perform（动词）。常见搭配：job performance / improve performance。
phrases.example: Error rates stayed stable in student performance. 学生作文的错误率保持稳定。

phrases.meaning: 遭受（suffer sth）；受苦（suffer from）

注意区分：performance（表现）/ perform（动词）。
注意区分：suffer sth（遭受，及物）/ suffer from（患……病）。
analysis.paragraphRole: 开篇为「冒充者现象」下定义，直接亮出这类人最核心的特征——长期低估自己，为全篇立论。

sentences.text: They think that any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance.

analysis.translationLiteral: 他们认为任何成功都归因于外部环境，或者仅仅是运气与偶然。
analysis.translationNatural: 在他们眼里，凡是成绩都得算在外部条件或干脆是走运头上，跟自己没关系。
analysis.structMarkup: 【They】 _think_ {that any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance}.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓 + that 引导的宾语从句；从句为主系表，due to 介词短语作表语，or 并列两类外因。

components.note: 回指上句 People，泛指有此类倾向的人
及物动词，后接 that 宾语从句引出其看法

components.part: that any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance
components.note: 作 think 的宾语，陈述他们把成功一律外推的归因方式

components.part: due to external circumstances or just luck and chance
components.note: due to 短语在从句中作表语，or 并列「外部环境」与「运气偶然」

clauses: 宾语从句「that any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and cha」：作 think 的宾语，陈述他们把成功一律外推的归因方式
that 引导宾语从句，作前面动词的宾语，从句用陈述语序。

phrases.meaning: 由于、因为
phrases.usage: 介词短语，后接名词；比 because of 更书面，常作表语或状语。

phrases.meaning: 想、认为；思考

phrases.example: Many think the risk is small. 很多人认为风险很小。

phrases.meaning: 成功、成就
phrases.usage: 常见搭配：achieve success / the key to success。
phrases.example: Hard work is not the only route to success. 努力并非成功的唯一路径。

pitfalls: due to 后接名词，不能接句子。
宾语从句用陈述语序，不要把助动词提到主语前。
analysis.paragraphRole: 承接定义，揭示这类人解释成功的固定套路：一律归给外因，正是第46题要辨别的态度。

sentences.text: Those people live in constant fear that their "deception" will be exposed.

analysis.translationLiteral: 那些人活在持续的恐惧里，生怕他们所谓的「欺骗」有朝一日被揭穿。
analysis.translationNatural: 他们成天提心吊胆，总怕自己「冒牌」的底细哪天被当众戳破。
analysis.structMarkup: 【Those people】 _live in constant fear_ {that their "deception" will be exposed}.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓结构 + in 介词短语作状语；that 引导同位语从句具体说明 fear 的内容，从句用被动语态。

components.note: 指示词 Those 加名词，回指前文所描述的那群人
live 作谓语，in constant fear 描摹其长期所处的心境
介词短语作状语，意为「处于挥之不去的恐惧中」
补充说明 fear 的具体内容；引号给「欺骗」添上自嘲式距离，从句用将来时被动

clauses: 同位语从句「that their "deception" will be exposed」：补充说明 fear 的具体内容；引号给「欺骗」添上自嘲式距离，从句用将来时被动
be + 过去分词构成被动语态，主语是动作的承受者。

phrases.meaning: 人们（复数集合名词，谓语用复数）；民族（可数）
phrases.usage: 注意区分：people（人们，复数）/ person（一个人）/ peoples（多个民族）。常见搭配：young people / people in business。
phrases.example: Most people agree on this point. 多数人同意这一点。

phrases.meaning: 持续的、不变的
phrases.usage: 注意区分：constant（持续不断的；恒定不变的）/ continuous（连续不间断的）/ continual（频繁发生、时断时续的）/ constant 与 consistent（前者「不变/不停」，后者「前后一致」）。常见搭配：constant exercise / under constant pressure。

phrases.meaning: 恐惧、害怕、担忧；畏惧、恐怕、担心
phrases.usage: 注意区分：fear（害怕、恐惧，名词/动词）/ fear of（对…的恐惧，介词 of）/ for fear that/of（唯恐，从句常用 should/might）/ fear to do（不敢做）/ afraid（只作表语，be afraid of，不说 an afraid boy）。

pitfalls: 被动语态的过去分词不能误写成过去式；不及物动词没有被动。
注意区分：people（人们，复数）/ person（一个人）/ peoples（多个民族）。
注意区分：constant（持续不断的；恒定不变的）/ continuous（连续不间断的）/ continual（频繁发生、时断时续的）/ constant 与 consistent（前者「不变/不停」，后者「前后一致」）。
analysis.paragraphRole: 补上这类人的心理状态：因怕被拆穿而长期焦虑，把定义里的「冒充」二字坐实，呼应第46题。

paragraphs.text: It is common for people to question their abilities now and again. A healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt can protect a person from acting impulsively. However, there are people who are permanently plagued by a massive amount of self-doubt despite delivering a good performance. They think that all of their successes are not a product of their skill or hard work, instead they attribute their own successes to external circumstances, for example, to luck and chance, or believe that their performance is massively overestimated by others. Failures, on the other hand, are always internalised as the result of their own shortcomings.

sentences.text: It is common for people to question their abilities now and again.

analysis.translationLiteral: 人们时不时地质疑自己的能力，这是很常见的。
analysis.translationNatural: 偶尔怀疑一下自己几斤几两，其实人人都会有，再正常不过。
analysis.structMarkup: 【It】 _is_ ~common~ 【for people to question their abilities now and again】.
analysis.structureSummary: It 作形式主语 + 系表结构；真正主语是句末 for people to question... 的不定式复合结构。

components.note: 占位的形式主语，无实义，真正主语在句末不定式
连接形式主语与表语 common
形容词作表语，判断这种情况「很常见」

components.part: for people to question their abilities now and again
components.note: for + 名词 + 不定式构成真正主语，说明谁、做什么
频度副词短语，强调「偶尔、时不时」

clauses: 本句是简单句，没有从句；主干为「It 作形式主语 + 系表结构；真正主语是句末 for people to question... 的不定式复合结构。」。

phrases.meaning: 常见的、普遍的；共同的
phrases.usage: 注意区分：common（常见/共同）/ ordinary（普通）/ usual（通常的）。常见搭配：in common / common sense。
phrases.example: Paternity leave is becoming more common. 陪产假越来越普遍。

phrases.meaning: 人们（复数集合名词，谓语用复数）；民族（可数）
phrases.usage: 注意区分：people（人们，复数）/ person（一个人）/ peoples（多个民族）。常见搭配：young people / people in business。
phrases.example: Most people agree on this point. 多数人同意这一点。

phrases.meaning: 问题（需回答）；疑问 / 质疑
phrases.usage: 注意区分：question（疑问）/ problem（难题）/ out of the question（不可能）。常见搭配：ask a question / the question is。
phrases.example: This seemingly easy question drives the need to understand. 这个看似简单的问题催生了理解的需要。

pitfalls: 注意区分：common（常见/共同）/ ordinary（普通）/ usual（通常的）。
注意区分：people（人们，复数）/ person（一个人）/ peoples（多个民族）。
注意区分：question（疑问）/ problem（难题）/ out of the question（不可能）。
analysis.paragraphRole: 本段先立一个常识靶子：偶发的自我怀疑人人都有，为下文区分「健康」与「病态」做铺垫。

sentences.text: A healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt can protect a person from acting impulsively.

analysis.translationLiteral: 适度的反思与自我怀疑能够防止一个人冲动行事。
analysis.translationNatural: 适度的反思和自我怀疑反而是好事，能让人不至于一时冲动。
analysis.structMarkup: 【A healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt】 _can protect_ ~a person~ (from acting impulsively).
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓宾结构；情态动词 can + protect，后接 protect...from... 搭配，from 后为动名词短语。

components.part: A healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt
components.note: 名词短语作主语，healthy amount 限定为「适度」而非过度
情态动词 can + 动词原形，表「能够起到保护作用」
protect 的宾语，指被保护的对象
protect...from... 固定搭配，from 后接动名词，说明免于何种行为

clauses: 本句是简单句，没有从句；主干为「主谓宾结构；情态动词 can + protect，后接 protect...from... 搭配，from 后为动名词短语。」。

phrases.meaning: 健康的；有益健康的
phrases.usage: 注意区分：healthy（健康的）/ healthful（有益健康的）/ health（健康，名词）。常见搭配：a healthy diet / healthy habits。
phrases.example: They start a healthy diet. 他们开始健康饮食。

phrases.meaning: 数量（不可数）；总额 / 合计为
phrases.usage: 注意区分：amount of（接不可数）/ number of（接可数）。常见搭配：a large amount of / the amount of。
phrases.example: They share the same amount of care. 他们承担同等数量的照护。

phrases.meaning: 保护（protect sb from sth）

phrases.example: Law can protect minors online. 法律可以保护网上未成年人。

pitfalls: 注意区分：healthy（健康的）/ healthful（有益健康的）/ health（健康，名词）。
注意区分：amount of（接不可数）/ number of（接可数）。
注意区分：protect from/against（保护免受）/ prevention（预防）。
analysis.paragraphRole: 正面说明「适度自我怀疑」的益处——防止冲动，对应第47题的正确选项。

sentences.text: However, there are people who are permanently plagued by a massive amount of self-doubt despite delivering a good performance.

analysis.translationLiteral: 然而，也有人尽管交出了不错的表现，却长期被大量的自我怀疑所折磨。
analysis.translationNatural: 可偏偏有一类人，成绩明明不差，却常年被铺天盖地的自我怀疑缠着不放。
analysis.structMarkup: (However), _there are_ 【people】 {who are permanently plagued by a massive amount of self-doubt} (despite delivering a good performance).

there be 存在句，真正主语是 people 及其定语从句

phrases.meaning: 人们（复数集合名词，谓语用复数）；民族（可数）
phrases.usage: 注意区分：people（人们，复数）/ person（一个人）/ peoples（多个民族）。常见搭配：young people / people in business。
phrases.example: Most people agree on this point. 多数人同意这一点。

phrases.meaning: 数量（不可数）；总额 / 合计为
phrases.usage: 注意区分：amount of（接不可数）/ number of（接可数）。常见搭配：a large amount of / the amount of。
phrases.example: They share the same amount of care. 他们承担同等数量的照护。

analysis.paragraphRole: 用 However 一转，点出与「适度」相对的另一极：表现良好却仍长期重度自我怀疑，界定病态人群。

sentences.text: They think that all of their successes are not a product of their skill or hard work, instead they attribute their own successes to external circumstances, for example, to luck and chance, or believe that their performance is massively overestimated by others.

analysis.translationLiteral: 他们认为自己所有的成功都不是其技能或努力的产物，反而把自己的成功归因于外部环境，例如运气与偶然，或者认为自己的表现被他人大大高估了。

that 引导宾语从句，作前面动词的宾语，从句用陈述语序。

phrases.meaning: 例如
phrases.usage: 插入语，常用逗号隔开，可置于句首、句中或句末。

phrases.meaning: 想、认为；思考
phrases.usage: 注意区分：think about（考虑）/ think of（想起）/ think over（仔细考虑）。常见搭配：think about / think of。

sentences.text: Failures, on the other hand, are always internalised as the result of their own shortcomings.

analysis.translationLiteral: 而失败，在另一方面，则总是被内化为他们自身缺点的结果。
analysis.translationNatural: 可一遇到失败，他们又照单全收，认定全是自己不行所致。

paragraphs.text: The study showed two things: First, the self-reported degree of Impostor Phenomenon is not related to actual measured intelligence or performance. Secondly, the test supported the assumption that people with a tendency to exhibit the Impostor Phenomenon devalue their objectively measured performance and attribute positive results to external causes such as luck and chance, but not to their own abilities. These results are also completely unrelated to age and gender.

paragraphs.text: A permanent underestimation of one's own abilities is often accompanied by the fear that this supposed intellectual deception will be exposed sooner or later and that they will pay the price for this. The Impostor Phenomenon was first described in 1978 by US psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes. They observed that there is a particularly high number of successful women who do not think they are very intelligent. The Impostor Phenomenon is not defined as a mental illness. However, people who suffer from it show a higher vulnerability to depression.

phrases.usage: 本句中作num./adj./adv.，可按「主谓（被动语态）+ in 1978 时间状语 + by 短语引出施事者；first 作状语。」定位它在句中的位置。
phrases.example: The Impostor Phenomenon was first described in 1978 by US psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes. 这一概念最早由美国心理学家 Pauline Clance 与 Suzanne Imes 在 1978 年提出。

pitfalls: 注意区分：psychologists（复数/三单）/ psychologist（原形）。
by US psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes：by 引出施事，US psychologists 后接两人姓名作同位说明
analysis.paragraphRole: 插入概念史：点明 1978 年由两位美国心理学家首次提出，为第50题定位出处。

sentences.text: They observed that there is a particularly high number of successful women who do not think they are very intelligent.

analysis.translationLiteral: 他们观察到，有相当多的成功女性并不认为自己很聪明。
analysis.translationNatural: 两位学者发现，事业有成的女性里，有特别多的人压根不觉得自己聪明。
analysis.structMarkup: 【They】 _observed_ {that there is a particularly high number of successful women who do not think they are very intelligent}.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓 + that 宾语从句；从句为 there be 存在句，主语后接 who 定语从句，从句内又含 think 的宾语从句。

components.note: 回指上句两位心理学家
及物动词过去式，后接 that 宾语从句

components.part: that there is a particularly high number of successful women who do not think they are very intelligent
components.note: observed 的宾语，陈述其观察到的现象

components.part: who do not think they are very intelligent
components.note: who 修饰 successful women，从句内省略 that 的宾语从句说明自我认知

clauses: 宾语从句「that there is a particularly high number of successful women who do no」：observed 的宾语，陈述其观察到的现象
定语从句「who do not think they are very intelligent」：who 修饰 successful women，从句内省略 that 的宾语从句说明自我认知
There be 句型中 there 是引导词，真正的主语在 be 之后，谓语与之一致。

phrases.meaning: 观察、注意到、看到；遵守；评论、说（observe 的过去式）
phrases.usage: 注意区分：observe（观察；遵守；评论，及物）/ observe sb do（看到全过程）与 observe sb doing（看到正在做）/ notice（无意中注意到）/ observation（观察，名词）/ observe a rule（遵守规则）。
phrases.example: They observed that there is a particularly high number of successful women who do not think they are very intelligent. 两位学者发现，事业有成的女性里，有特别多的人压根不觉得自己聪明。

phrases.meaning: 高的；高度的 / 高高地
phrases.usage: 注意区分：high（具体高）/ highly（抽象程度高，如 highly likely）。常见搭配：high school / high rates。
phrases.example: Isolation is linked to higher rates of disease. 孤立与更高发病率相关。

phrases.meaning: 数字、数量；号码
phrases.usage: 注意区分：a number of（许多，谓语复数）/ the number of（数量，谓语单数）。常见搭配：a number of（许多） / the number of（……的数量）。
phrases.example: A number of studies agree. 许多研究结论一致。

pitfalls: There be 句型谓语的单复数跟 be 后面的名词走。
定语从句中关系词已充当成分，从句里不要再重复该代词。
analysis.paragraphRole: 补述当年观察到的典型人群——成功却不自信的女性，丰富概念背景，也呼应「低估自我」主题。

sentences.text: The Impostor Phenomenon is not defined as a mental illness.

analysis.translationLiteral: 冒充者现象并未被界定为一种精神疾病。
analysis.translationNatural: 严格说来，它并不算一种精神疾病。
analysis.structMarkup: 【The Impostor Phenomenon】 _is not defined_ (as a mental illness).
analysis.structureSummary: 主系表（被动否定）+ as 介词短语作补语。

components.note: 概念名作主语
被动否定式，意为「未被界定为」
as 短语说明界定的类别，明确「不是精神疾病」

clauses: 本句是简单句，没有从句；主干为「主系表（被动否定）+ as 介词短语作补语。」。

phrases.meaning: 心理的、精神的；脑力的
phrases.usage: 注意区分：mental（心理的）/ physical（身体的）。常见搭配：mental health / mental illness。
phrases.example: Social support improves mental health. 社会支持改善心理健康。

phrases.meaning: 界定、给…下定义、阐明（define 过去式/分词）；明确的、轮廓分明的
phrases.usage: 本句中作v./adj.，可按「主系表（被动否定）+ as 介词短语作补语。」定位它在句中的位置。
phrases.example: The Impostor Phenomenon is not defined as a mental illness. 严格说来，它并不算一种精神疾病。

pitfalls: 注意区分：mental（心理的）/ physical（身体的）。
as a mental illness：as 短语说明界定的类别，明确「不是精神疾病」
analysis.paragraphRole: 给出临床界定上的关键澄清：它不算精神疾病，为下句的转折蓄势。

sentences.text: However, people who suffer from it show a higher vulnerability to depression.

analysis.translationLiteral: 然而，受其困扰的人表现出对抑郁更高的易感性。
analysis.translationNatural: 不过，有这种倾向的人，确实更容易陷入抑郁。
analysis.structMarkup: (However), 【people】 {who suffer from it} _show_ ~a higher vulnerability to depression~.
analysis.structureSummary: However 转折状语 + 主谓宾；主语后 who 定语从句，宾语含比较级 higher。

components.note: 转折副词，与上句「不是疾病」形成对照
泛指受此困扰的人群
who 修饰 people，it 回指冒充者现象
及物动词，意为「表现出」
show 的宾语，比较级 higher 点明「更易抑郁」

clauses: 定语从句「who suffer from it」：who 修饰 people，it 回指冒充者现象
本句主干为「However 转折状语 + 主谓宾；主语后 who 定语从句，宾语含比较级 higher。」，先找限定动词再切分修饰成分。

phrases.meaning: 然而（副词，须用分号或句号连接）；无论怎样
phrases.usage: 注意区分：however（副词，不能像 but 那样直接连两个分句）/ but（连词）。常见搭配：however, ... / however much。
phrases.example: However, the study also shows a gap. 然而，研究也显示出一道差距。

phrases.meaning: 人们（复数集合名词，谓语用复数）；民族（可数）
phrases.usage: 注意区分：people（人们，复数）/ person（一个人）/ peoples（多个民族）。常见搭配：young people / people in business。
phrases.example: Most people agree on this point. 多数人同意这一点。

phrases.meaning: 遭受（suffer sth）；受苦（suffer from）
phrases.usage: 注意区分：suffer sth（遭受，及物）/ suffer from（患……病）。常见搭配：suffer an injury / suffer from。
phrases.example: Local farmers will suffer under this situation. 当地农民会在此情形下受损。

pitfalls: 注意区分：however（副词，不能像 but 那样直接连两个分句）/ but（连词）。
注意区分：people（人们，复数）/ person（一个人）/ peoples（多个民族）。
注意区分：suffer sth（遭受，及物）/ suffer from（患……病）。
analysis.paragraphRole: 以 However 收束全文，落到最实在的代价：虽非疾病，却更易抑郁——正是第50题的答案。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the passage about people who suffer from the so-called Impostor Phenomenon?

options.text: They systematically underestimate their chances of success.
They tend to attribute their achievements to good fortune.
They seem to live in constant fear of being deceived.
They generally rely on luck and chance for success.

questions.stem: What do people with a healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt tend to do?

options.text: Credit all their successes to hard work.
Strive hard to perfect their skills.
Refrain from acting on impulse.
Deliver a better performance.

questions.stem: What do Impostor Phenomenon sufferers often do according to psychologists from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg?

options.text: Attribute their accomplishments to others.
Deny their actual measured intelligence.
Claim to have confidence in their own abilities.
Mark down their objectively rated performance.

questions.stem: What happens when a person permanently underestimates their own abilities?

options.text: They will focus their attention on external factors.
They will be fearful of potential consequences.
They will count on good fortune for success.
They will keep improving their own skills.

questions.stem: What did US psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes say about Impostor Phenomenon sufferers?

options.text: They are more liable to have depression.
They seldom realise their potential fully.
They will develop mental illnesses.
They will pay higher prices one day.

abilities.sense: 能力、才能、本领（ability 的复数）

more.roots: able（能够）+ -ity（名词后缀）+ -ies（复数，辅音 + y → ies）
more.confusables: abilities 指多种技能，ability 泛指能力；搭配都用 to do，不用 of doing

examples: It is common for people to question their abilities now and again. 偶尔怀疑一下自己几斤几两，其实人人都会有，再正常不过。

acting.sense: 行动、做事；表演、扮演；行为、法令（本文 consumers to not only demand change—but to act themselves 消费者不仅要呼吁改变，更要自己行动）（act 的现在分词/动名词形式）
examples: A healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt can protect a person from acting impulsively. 适度的反思和自我怀疑反而是好事，能让人不至于一时冲动。

more.confusables: acting（现在分词/动名词）/ act（原形）

actual.sense: 实际的、真实的、现存的（in actual fact 事实上）
examples: Seventy-six participants completed a range of intelligence tests and received positive feedback on them, regardless of their actual performance. 76 名受试做完一整套智力测试，不论真实成绩怎样，一律得到了夸奖式的好评。

more.confusables: actual / actually（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

examples: It is common for people to question their abilities now and again. 偶尔怀疑一下自己几斤几两，其实人人都会有，再正常不过。

age.sense: 年龄、年纪；时代、时期；变老、老化
examples: These results are also completely unrelated to age and gender. 而且这些结论跟年龄、性别也半点关系都没有。

more.confusables: age / agencies（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

always.sense: 总是、一直、永远；始终（本文指「总是成为他人的囚徒」）
examples: Failures, on the other hand, are always internalised as the result of their own shortcomings. 可一遇到失败，他们又照单全收，认定全是自己不行所致。

amount.sense: 数量（不可数）；总额 / 合计为
examples: They share the same amount of care. 他们承担同等数量的照护。

more.roots: a-（=ad- 朝向）+ mount（山，词根，同 mountain）→ 累积成堆 → 总量
more.confusables: amount of（接不可数）/ number of（接可数）

asked.sense: 问、询问；要求、请求；邀请（ask 的过去式/过去分词）
examples: They were then asked why they think they did so well. 接着研究者问他们：觉得自己考得这么好，原因是什么？

Secondly, the test supported the assumption that people with a tendency to exhibit the Impostor Phenomenon devalue their objectively measured performance and attribute positive results to external causes such as luck and chance, but not to their own abilities. 其二，实验印证了假设：越有冒充者倾向的人，越会看低自己实测的成绩，把好结果推给运气等外因，唯独不认自己的本事。

more.confusables: assumption / assumptions（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

examples: I believe he is right. 我认为他是对的。

causes.sense: 原因、起因、事业（cause 的复数）；导致、引起（第三人称单数）
examples: Secondly, the test supported the assumption that people with a tendency to exhibit the Impostor Phenomenon devalue their objectively measured performance and attribute positive results to external causes such as luck and chance, but not to their own abilities. 其二，实验印证了假设：越有冒充者倾向的人，越会看低自己实测的成绩，把好结果推给运气等外因，唯独不认自己的本事。

more.confusables: causes / cause（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

chance.sense: 机会、机遇；可能性、概率；偶然（by chance 碰巧）

more.confusables: chance（机会，可数；可能性，不可数）/ by chance（偶然，副词短语）/ take a chance（冒险）/ chance to do / have a chance of doing / chance 与 opportunity（较正式，指有利时机）/ chance 与 change 拼写易混

examples: They think that any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance. 在他们眼里，凡是成绩都得算在外部条件或干脆是走运头上，跟自己没关系。
Paternity leave is becoming more common. 陪产假越来越普遍。

more.confusables: common（常见/共同）/ ordinary（普通）/ usual（通常的）

completed.sense: complete 的过去式/过去分词（完成）；已完成的
examples: Two hundred teenagers completed the survey. 两百名青少年完成了调查。

more.confusables: completed（已完成）/ complete（完整的/完成）

examples: These results are also completely unrelated to age and gender. 而且这些结论跟年龄、性别也半点关系都没有。

more.confusables: completely / completed / complete（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

conditions.sense: 条件；状况、病症（condition 的复数）
examples: Isolation is linked to mental health conditions. 孤立与心理健康问题相关。

more.confusables: condition（状况/病症）/ situation（情形）/ state（状态）

examples: Constant practice makes perfect. 持续练习才能熟能生巧。

more.roots: con-（加强）+ st（站立，词根 sta = stand，同 stand/stable/status）+ -ant
more.confusables: constant（持续不断的；恒定不变的）/ continuous（连续不间断的）/ continual（频繁发生、时断时续的）/ constant 与 consistent（前者「不变/不停」，后者「前后一致」）

defined.sense: 界定、给…下定义、阐明（define 过去式/分词）；明确的、轮廓分明的
examples: The Impostor Phenomenon is not defined as a mental illness. 严格说来，它并不算一种精神疾病。

more.confusables: defined / define / definition（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

examples: The study showed two things: First, the self-reported degree of Impostor Phenomenon is not related to actual measured intelligence or performance. 研究得出两个结论：其一，一个人自评有多「冒充者」，跟他实测的智力、成绩压根不挂钩。

more.confusables: degree（程度；学位；度，可数）/ to some / a certain degree（在某种程度上，= to some extent）/ by degrees（逐渐地）/ a bachelor's degree（学士学位）/ degree 与 diploma（diploma 是「文凭」，degree 是「学位」）

delivering.sense: 递送、交付、发表、兑现、实现；接生（本文 actually deliver your desired outcome 真正带来你想要的结果 / deliver a speech）（deliver 的现在分词/动名词形式）
examples: However, there are people who are permanently plagued by a massive amount of self-doubt despite delivering a good performance. 可偏偏有一类人，成绩明明不差，却常年被铺天盖地的自我怀疑缠着不放。

more.confusables: delivering（现在分词/动名词）/ deliver（原形）

described.sense: 描述、描写、形容（describe 的过去式/过去分词；be described as 被称作、被说成）
examples: The Impostor Phenomenon was first described in 1978 by US psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes. 这一概念最早由美国心理学家 Pauline Clance 与 Suzanne Imes 在 1978 年提出。

more.confusables: described / describe（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

despite.sense: 尽管、虽然（后接名词或动名词，不接从句）
examples: Despite progress, women still struggle. 尽管有进步，女性仍在艰难争取。

more.confusables: despite + 名词（不是从句）/ although + 从句

due.sense: 预期的、到期的；（due to）由于
examples: The change is due to new law. 这一变化源于新法律。

more.confusables: due to（由于，介词短语）/ because of（同义）/ be due to do（预计做）

examined.sense: examine 的过去式，考察、研究、检查
examples: Psychologists from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg examined the topic for the first time under real-life conditions. 哈勒-维滕贝格马丁·路德大学的心理学者头一回把这一现象搬到真实情境里做研究。

more.confusables: examined / examine / examination（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

examples: For example, texting and reading coexist. 例如，发短信和读书并存。

more.confusables: for example（插入语，缩写 e.g.）/ such as（后接名词）

external.sense: 外部的、外来的、外界的、外表的

more.roots: extern（外部，词根 exter = outward，同 exterior/extra/extreme）+ -al（形容词后缀）
more.confusables: external（外部的、外来的，如 external factors）/ internal（内部的，反义）/ exterior / interior（多指建筑物内外或人的外表/内心）/ external 与 outer（更口语，只指位置）

examples: They think that any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance. 在他们眼里，凡是成绩都得算在外部条件或干脆是走运头上，跟自己没关系。

failures.sense: 失败、不成功；失败的人 / 事；故障、失灵；未能做到（failure to do 未做…）（failure 的复数/三单形式）
examples: Failures, on the other hand, are always internalised as the result of their own shortcomings. 可一遇到失败，他们又照单全收，认定全是自己不行所致。

more.confusables: failures（复数/三单）/ failure（原形）

fear.sense: 恐惧、害怕、担忧；畏惧、恐怕、担心

more.confusables: fear（害怕、恐惧，名词/动词）/ fear of（对…的恐惧，介词 of）/ for fear that/of（唯恐，从句常用 should/might）/ fear to do（不敢做）/ afraid（只作表语，be afraid of，不说 an afraid boy）

examples: Those people live in constant fear that their "deception" will be exposed. 他们成天提心吊胆，总怕自己「冒牌」的底细哪天被当众戳破。

gender.sense: 性别；（语法的）性（gender differences 性别差异；gender gap 性别鸿沟）
examples: These results are also completely unrelated to age and gender. 而且这些结论跟年龄、性别也半点关系都没有。

more.confusables: gender / genders（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

good.sense: 好的；有益的 / 好处（不可数）

more.confusables: good at（擅长）/ good for（对……有益）/ well（副词，身体好）

hand.sense: 手；帮助（give sb a hand）/ 递（动词）

examples: They think that all of their successes are not a product of their skill or hard work, instead they attribute their own successes to external circumstances, for example, to luck and chance, or believe that their performance is massively overestimated by others. 他们觉得成绩跟本事、跟下过的功夫统统无关，反倒一股脑推给外部条件——比方说走运；再不然就认定，别人把他们的水平抬得过高了。

more.confusables: hard / harder / hardware（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

more.confusables: healthy（健康的）/ healthful（有益健康的）/ health（健康，名词）

high.sense: 高的；高度的 / 高高地

more.confusables: high（具体高）/ highly（抽象程度高，如 highly likely）

higher.sense: 更高的（high 的比较级）；更高地

however.sense: 然而（副词，须用分号或句号连接）；无论怎样

more.confusables: however（副词，不能像 but 那样直接连两个分句）/ but（连词）

illness.sense: 疾病、生病、病痛（ill 的名词形式；a serious illness 重病）
examples: The Impostor Phenomenon is not defined as a mental illness. 严格说来，它并不算一种精神疾病。
